proposed_comments.title: Retain a stop request across delayed watcher startup (4/4)

confidence.rationale: Actual watcher source with a namespace-local delayed Thread adapter: 6.5-second startup delay; upstream Stop still blocked at 9 seconds (exit 42), candidate completed in 6517ms (exit 0). No live input/dialog interaction was simulated.

proposed_comments.body:
### Retain a stop request across delayed watcher startup (4/4)

**Severity:** `high`

The five-second readiness wait can expire before the worker creates its queue. Stop then misses WM_QUIT and blocks in Join after the worker eventually enters GetMessage. Keep a volatile stop request, reset it only when starting a worker, set it before waiting, and check it before entering the message pump. Apply all four watcher edits together.

```suggestion
            while (!_stopRequested && GetMessageW(out NativeMessage msg, IntPtr.Zero, 0, 0) > 0)
```

proposed_comments.title: Do not replace an unreadable device-profile document (5/5)

confidence.rationale: Verbatim storage sources with private path/event adapters: malformed and null documents were overwritten upstream; candidate Save returned false and preserved bytes. Missing-file creation and valid-hotkey round-trip passed both.

proposed_comments.body:
### Do not replace an unreadable device-profile document (5/5)

**Severity:** `high`

Save uses the tolerant Load result to preserve cycleHotkey. If the existing document is malformed or JSON null at save time, Load supplies an empty object and Save replaces the original bytes and hotkey with a fresh document. Use strict reads for update paths and let their existing error handlers reject the update. Retain tolerant reads for display-only callers and creation when the file is absent. Apply all five edits together.

```suggestion
            catch (Exception ex) when (!strict)
```

proposed_comments.title: Serialize complete settings read-modify-write transactions

confidence.rationale: Controlled interleaving of two actual ReadSettingsRoot snapshots and WriteSettingsRoot commits loses the first writer's active profile on both trees. This demonstrates the storage interleaving, not end-to-end UI scheduling.

proposed_comments.body:
### Serialize complete settings read-modify-write transactions

**Severity:** `high`

The new profile operations read settings.json and later replace its full content without coordinating with the engine or the Settings app. The engine mutex serializes only its own switching workers, while the Settings view model rereads profile fields before sending a full payload; neither covers the other process's commit. Two snapshots can therefore overwrite one another's active profile or configuration-list changes. Please use a shared cross-process transaction lock (or a single owner) across every reader/writer transaction, re-read the latest document while holding it, preserve unrelated fields, check write success, and release it only after persistence. If replacing files atomically, also update the editor watcher to observe replacements; atomic rename alone does not prevent lost updates.

proposed_comments.title: Make profile deletion transactional across its stores

confidence.rationale: Injected membership-save failure against actual ProfileManager deletes Work.json and still returns true on both upstream and candidate. Membership helper is an injected failure adapter, not the complete running editor.

proposed_comments.body:
### Make profile deletion transactional across its stores

**Severity:** `high`

DeleteProfile removes the profile config before attempting membership, device-assignment, metadata and settings cleanup. A membership write failure is only logged, device pruning returns no success result, and the method can still return true with incomplete cleanup. Please stage the store updates before deleting the config, propagate every persistence failure, and restore the prior config and metadata if a later commit fails; return success and signal reload only after the coordinated commit completes. Returning false after the current early deletion alone would not restore the lost config.

proposed_comments.title: Validate profile IDs before using config paths

confidence.rationale: Actual ProfileManager source in private fixture: DeleteProfile("settings") returned true and erased the sentinel upstream; candidate rejected it and preserved the sentinel. Selection uses the same existing validator.

proposed_comments.body:
### Validate profile IDs before using config paths

**Severity:** `high`

GetProfiles trusts keyboardConfigurations entries even though the directory scan filters reserved stems. A persisted settings entry can therefore expose settings as a profile, and DeleteProfile then removes settings.json before rewriting a default settings object. Reuse IsValidProfileName at the selection and deletion entry points, keeping reserved stores and invalid filename stems out of config-path operations.

```suggestion
            if (!IsValidProfileName(profile) || profile.Equals(DefaultProfile, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
```

proposed_comments.title: Keep typed key values out of device-resolution diagnostics

confidence.rationale: Exact source ordering and formatting argument inspected; final engine build compiles the literal replacement. No production user keystrokes collected.

proposed_comments.body:
### Keep typed key values out of device-resolution diagnostics

**Severity:** `medium`

An unresolved keyboard path logs the virtual-key value for each keydown before checking whether auto-switch is enabled. Trace logs can therefore contain a sequence of typed keys even when the feature is disabled. Retain the device-resolution diagnostic without the virtual-key value.

```suggestion
        Logger::trace(L"[autosw] unresolvable keyboard device - skipped");
```

proposed_comments.title: Observe cancellation before entering the worker message pump

confidence.rationale: Verbatim native worker sources with controlled API startup delay of 6.5 seconds: tracker/hotkey upstream exit 42 after stuck joins, candidate exit 0 in 6551ms/6632ms. Logger/PCH are fixture stubs.

proposed_comments.body:
### Observe cancellation before entering the worker message pump

**Severity:** `high`

If startup exceeds Stop's five-second readiness wait, WM_QUIT can be posted before a message queue exists. The resumed worker then blocks in GetMessage and Stop remains stuck in join. Check the existing atomic m_started flag before GetMessage. Stop already clears it before waiting, so a late-starting worker skips the pump and reaches its existing cleanup.

```suggestion
    while (m_started.load() && GetMessageW(&msg, nullptr, 0, 0) > 0)
```
